title: Focker In-Law Review Finds Ariana Grande the Standout in a Tired Fourth Film
excerpt:
A new review criticizes the franchise's recycled comedy.
Ariana Grande and Owen Wilson nevertheless emerge as highlights.
body_md:
The Meet the Parents comedy franchise returns with Focker In-Law, its fourth installment and first in sixteen years. A Hollywood Reporter review argues that the series has continued to lose its comic momentum, although the assessment is the critic's opinion rather than a measure of audience consensus.

Ben Stiller's Greg Focker has become a suspicious parent himself. His son Henry, played by Skyler Gisondo, brings girlfriend Olivia, played by Ariana Grande, to a gathering for Jack's eightieth birthday. Greg distrusts the relationship, putting him in a role resembling the one Robert De Niro's Jack occupied in the original film.

The critic takes issue with the film's repeated humiliation-based set pieces. An airplane misunderstanding, Jack's vegan diet, a dog named Lorenzo, and a stolen engagement ring all figure in Greg's increasingly elaborate efforts to derail Henry's proposal. The review finds many of these incidents implausible and overextended.

John Hamburg, a writer on the preceding three installments, directs and writes this entry. The reported runtime is one hour and forty-five minutes, and the film carries a PG-13 rating. Its listed release date is November 25, 2026.

Grande's Olivia, described as a former FBI hostage negotiator, is singled out for her deadpan delivery and ability to hold her own opposite experienced comic actors. Owen Wilson also earns praise for his understated return as Kevin Rawley. Other returning and new cast members include Teri Polo, Blythe Danner, Beanie Feldstein and Eduardo Franco.

The central distinction in the review is between the film's execution and its performers. The critic sees a tired formula and underused supporting players, while finding Grande's performance a compelling reason to pay attention.
